facts.text: There are no rules in a family, but there are norms; schools have rules about admission, uniform and studies.

facts.text: Rules about family, school, village or city are limited, but provisions about the administration of a country are much wider in scope.
facts.quote: The rules regarding family, school, village or city are limited in nature. But the rules or provisions about the administration of a country are much wider in scope.

facts.text: The book in which all the provisions regarding the administration of a country are mentioned together in a systematic way is called a Constitution.
facts.quote: The book in which all the provisions regarding the administration of a the country are mentioned together in a systematic way is called a Constitution.

facts.text: A Constitution is a written document of the provisions related to the administration of the country.
facts.quote: This makes the Constitution a written document of the provisions related to the administration of the country.

facts.text: Government is established by representatives elected by the people and is bound to carry out administration as per the Constitution.
facts.quote: Government is established by the representatives elected by the people. It is bound to carry out the administration of the country as per the provisions of the Constitution.

facts.text: The rules and provisions in the Constitution are the basic or fundamental law of the land.
facts.quote: The rules and provisions in the Constitution are the basic or fundamental law of the land.

facts.text: While making laws the government is bound to follow the Constitution; if it does not, the Judiciary can declare those laws null and void or unconstitutional.
facts.quote: While making laws, the government is bound to follow the Constitution. If it does not do so, then the Judiciary can declare those laws null and void or unconstitutional.

facts.text: Provisions in the Constitution are about citizenship, rights of citizens, the relationship between citizens and the State, subjects of laws, elections, restrictions on government and jurisdiction of the State.
facts.quote: The provisions in the Constitution are about different things, e.g., citizenship, the rights of citizens, the relationship between citizens and the State, subjects of the laws to be made by the governments, elections, restrictions on government, jurisdiction of the State, etc.

facts.text: Almost all countries accept governance according to a Constitution, but the nature of Constitutions differs because of history, social structures, culture and traditions.
facts.quote: Almost all countries have accepted the principle of governance according to a Constitution. Yet the nature of the Constitutions of different countries is different. There are differences of history, social structures, culture, traditions, etc.

facts.text: The American Constitution came into force in 1789.

facts.text: The American Constitution is a written Constitution with only 7 articles; even after 225 years the American government follows it.

facts.text: In England the rules of running the country are found as conventions, norms and traditions; the English Constitution is considered primarily unwritten.
facts.quote: The rules of running the country here are found in the form of conventions, norms and traditions. ... the English Constitution is considered to be primarily unwritten.

facts.text: The Magna Carta of 1215 marks the beginning of the development of the English Constitution.
facts.quote: The Magna Carta of 1215 marks the beginning of the development of the English Constitution.

facts.text: Government has to function within a set of rules, which reduces the possibility of the misuse of power and authority.
facts.quote: Government has to function within a set of rules. This reduces the possibility of the misuse of the power and authority they have been given.

facts.text: A Constitution includes the rights and freedoms of citizens, which the government cannot take away.
facts.quote: A Constitution includes the rights and freedoms of the citizens. Government cannot take away these rights.

facts.text: Running a country as per the Constitution is the same as establishing the rule of law.
facts.quote: Running a country as per the provisions of the Constitution is the same as establishing the rule of law.

facts.text: When a country is run as per the Constitution, people's faith in government increases and democracy is strengthened by their participation.

facts.text: The Constitution presents political ideals and creates an atmosphere for world peace, security and preservation of human rights.
facts.quote: Constitution presents some political ideals before the country. ... It creates an atmosphere conducive to attain world peace and security and preservation of human rights.

facts.text: The Constitution includes the list of citizens' duties and so fixes their responsibility.

facts.text: Governments in modern times take decisions on issues right from space research to public cleanliness; this is governance or administration.

facts.text: The process of the making of the Indian Constitution started in 1946.
facts.quote: The process of the making of the Indian Constitution started in 1946.

facts.text: Leaders of the freedom movement insisted that Independent India be governed by laws made by Indians, not by the British.

facts.text: The committee established to prepare the Constitution of Independent India came to be known as the Constituent Assembly.
facts.quote: A Committee was established to prepare the Constitution of Independent India. It came to be known as the Constituent Assembly.

facts.text: India became independent on August 15, 1947.
facts.quote: India became independent on August 15, 1947.

facts.text: The British divided India into provinces like Bombay, Bengal and Madras for the convenience of administration.
facts.quote: They had divided India into provinces like Bombay, Bengal and Madras for the convenience of administration.

facts.text: Areas where local princes carried out administration were known as princely states, and their chiefs were known as princes.
facts.quote: Similarly, the local princes were carrying out the administration in some areas. Such areas were known as princely states and their chiefs were known as princes.

facts.text: Representatives of the provinces and the princely states were included in the Constituent Assembly.
facts.quote: The representatives of the provinces and the princely states were included in the Constituent Assembly.

facts.text: There were a total of 299 members in the Constituent Assembly.
facts.quote: There were a total of 299 members in the Constituent Assembly.

facts.text: Dr Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly.

facts.quote: Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. He had studied in depth, the Constitutions of different countries of the world.

facts.text: The draft Constitution was discussed Article by Article and many amendments were suggested by members.

facts.text: Due to his contribution, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar is called the 'Architect of the Indian Constitution'.
facts.quote: Due to his contribution towards the making of the Constitution, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar is called the 'Architect of the Indian Constitution.'

facts.text: Decisions in the Constituent Assembly were made on the basis of debate and discussion, with respect for opposing viewpoints.
facts.quote: Decisions in the Constituent Assembly were made on the basis of debate and discussion. A respect for opposing viewpoints and acceptance of appropriate suggestions was a characteristic of the working of the Constituent Assembly.

facts.text: It took 2 years, 11 months and 17 days to complete the writing of the Constitution.
facts.quote: It took 2 years, 11 months and 17 days to complete the writing of the Constitution.

facts.text: The original Constitution had 22 parts, 395 articles and 8 schedules.
facts.quote: There were 22 parts, 395 articles and 8 schedules in the original Constitution.

facts.quote: The noted legal expert, B. N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional Adviser on legal matters.

facts.text: 26th November is observed as Constitution Day.

facts.text: The country began to be governed according to the Constitution from 26th January 1950, and the Indian Republic came into existence.
